name: Eastern Express Highway
aka: City stretch of the old NH 3 (Mumbai–Agra Road)
lanes: Mostly 6 lanes (3 each way), with more than a dozen flyovers and grade separators

timeline.event: The Eastern Freeway is completed and drops onto the highway at Chheda Nagar, Ghatkopar
MMRDA hands the highway to the BMC for upkeep (3 October)
Maharashtra scraps the entry toll for cars at Mumbai's five booths, including the one at Mulund on this road

history: The Eastern Express Highway connects Sion in Mumbai with the city of Thane, running through the eastern suburbs. It was built as the city end of the old Mumbai–Agra national highway, NH 3, at a time when factories were spreading fast through Thane and Bhiwandi and the old roads could not cope. Over the years it was widened to six lanes and given more than a dozen flyovers, so traffic can run for long stretches without meeting a signal. At Chheda Nagar in Ghatkopar it meets the Eastern Freeway, which gives the eastern suburbs a fast, toll-free run into south Mumbai. In October 2022 the MMRDA handed the road over to the city's municipal corporation, the BMC, to look after. Since October 2024 cars and other light vehicles no longer pay the old entry toll at the Mulund booth on this highway.
facts: About 23.5 km long, from Sion to Thane.
Was historically the starting stretch of NH 3, the Mumbai–Agra Road.
Meets the Eastern Freeway at Chheda Nagar, Ghatkopar.
Handed over to the city's municipal corporation (BMC) for upkeep in 2022.
Six lanes wide for most of its length, with over a dozen flyovers so through-traffic can skip the junctions.
One of Mumbai's five old entry toll booths sat on this road at Mulund; cars stopped paying there in October 2024.
At Mulund it links to the Airoli creek bridge, the shortest hop from the eastern suburbs to Navi Mumbai.
significance: This is the main road spine of Mumbai's eastern suburbs and the road by which much of the traffic from Nashik and northern Maharashtra reaches the city. Lakhs of commuters, buses and trucks use it every day, and it is the road that ties Thane — a city of its own — into Mumbai.

travelNotes: Sion to Thane is only 23 km but can take anywhere from 40 minutes to well over an hour and a half in peak traffic. The worst crawls are at Sion, Vikhroli, the Mulund check naka and the approach to Thane. Heavy rain floods low points near Sion and Vikhroli during the monsoon, and metro construction work along the route narrows the road in places.
futureUpgrades: Mumbai Metro Line 4 (Wadala–Kasarvadavali) is being built on pillars along much of the highway corridor.
The BMC has taken up resurfacing and bridge repairs along the highway since taking it over.
